Merz programming , artificial intelligence , ai , llm , web programming I can only speculate as to the reasons why I was laid off from Meta in May, but I suspect that one of the reasons is that I was a little bit more resistant to adopting AI/LLMs as coding tools than some of my peers. Don't get me wrong, I generated at least 90% of my code using AI in my last few months there, which was the minimum for a decent rating. But AI didn't 10X the amount of code I was writing. It didn't even 2X it. I was focused on code quality. I saw the code being pushed by some of my peers who were heavily reliant on AI, and I saw that it was brittle code. There were many subtle issues that would lead to tech debt in the long term, and even some glaring issues were ignored by very good programmers.
